summary: Misapplied hourly-tier discount during dedicated reserved capacity swap resulting in invoice line mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ClariData) reports a mismatch between expected discounted hourly line items and the finalized invoice after they performed a reserved-capacity swap (moved workload from an older reserved pool to a new reserved pool within the same billing cycle). Impact: customer sees an under-applied discount on 6 hours of reserved usage and an unexpected separate 'hosted fallback' line.

Impact:
- Invoice overcharge of ~$2,180 for billing period ending 2026-03-11 as reported by customer finance team.
- Affects one dedicated tenant during a reserve swap/zone migration.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east regional billing batch.
- Customer using Dedicated reserved capacity (contract ID RC-2025-CLARIDATA).

Observed behavior:
- During the reserve swap at 2026-03-10T18:20Z, postback ordering caused subset of traffic to be attributed to the old reserved tag for part of the hour and to hosted fallback for remaining requests. The hourly-tier discount rule matched only the new reserved tag for that hour, leaving a gap.

Expected behavior:
- Pricing tier logic should aggregate hourly usage across the swap window and apply the reserved hourly-tier discount pro rata, avoiding separate hosted fallback lines when traffic has a valid reserved mapping.

Requested outcome from customer:
- Reconciliation of the month invoice lines and application of compensatory credit for the under-applied discount.

Relevant account identifiers and billing metadata:
- Account: clari-data-prod (acct_0CLARIDA)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Perform a reserved capacity reassignment on a dedicated tenant during an hourly boundary (swap old-reserve -> new-reserve at 18:20Z).
2) Generate steady inference traffic to rw-13b-v2 from 18:00Z to 19:00Z to exercise hourly aggregation window.
3) Let billing postbacks run and finalize hourly aggregation job.
4) Compare resulting invoice lines to expected prorated reserved discount for 18:00-19:00 hour.
logs: 2026-03-10T18:19:59Z POSTBACK Received: tenant=acct_0CLARIDA tag=reserve_old usage=1200 tokens
2026-03-10T18:20:05Z POSTBACK Received: tenant=acct_0CLARIDA tag=reserve_new usage=800 tokens
2026-03-10T18:20:08Z POSTBACK Received: tenant=acct_0CLARIDA tag=hosted_fallback usage=400 tokens

Billing batch query (hourly_agg): SELECT sum(tokens) FROM postbacks WHERE tenant='acct_0CLARIDA' AND hour='2026-03-10T18:00Z' GROUP BY tag;  -- returned three groups (reserve_old, reserve_new, hosted_fallback)
comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Lin (Support): Created ticket after customer emailed billing@redwood. Included invoice snapshot and reserve swap timestamp.
2026-03-12 - Arjun Patel (Billing Eng): Acknowledged. I'll pull hourly_agg and check postback ordering and tolerant merge window logic. Assigned to Billing team for triage.

2026-03-13 - Billing Eng (Arjun Patel): Preliminary find: reconciliation service only applies hourly-tier discount when rule matches a single primary tag in the hour. If multiple tags present, we create separate invoice lines instead of collapsing under reserved-tier pro rata. This is working-as-coded but not desired for swap windows. Logged issue to reconciler PRs.
2026-03-13 - Customer (Emma Soto, ClariData Finance): Can you provide estimated credit amount? We need that for our month-end close.
2026-03-14 - Maya Lin (Support): Applied provisional credit of $2,180 to account as interim remedy (see note). Billing team to confirm exact reconciliation and final credit after fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Hourly aggregation logic treats tags atomically; when multiple tags appear in the hour aggregation it does not merge into a single prorated reserved line. This interacts poorly with reserve swaps that occur mid-hour.

Checked reconciler logs for hour 2026-03-10T18:00Z: three groups detected; discount_applier skipped pro rata computation because group_count > 1. See reconciler log pointer: /var/log/reconciler/2026-03-10/agg-18.log lines 412-436.

Ran local SQL to simulate desired pro rata: computed expected reserved_discount = (tokens_with_reserved_tags / total_tokens) * reserved_hourly_rate_discount -> results matched customer's expected reduction (~$2,180).

Related code paths: billing/discount_applier.py -> function apply_hourly_tier_discount; edge-case gating at line where groups>1 -> early return. Patch proposed to compute weighted prorate when groups are compatible (reserve_old + reserve_new + hosted_fallback where hosted_fallback had reserve mapping within 10s).

Potential side-effects: need to ensure we do not incorrectly apply reserved discount to true hosted traffic. Proposed guard: only merge groups if there is a matching reserve contract active for the tenant during hour and if hosted_fallback tag was observed only during overlap window and followed by reserved tag within X seconds.
resolution: Temporary actions: provisional credit of $2,180 applied on 2026-03-14 to clari-data-prod account (credit ID CR-2026-171). Long-term fix: billing team to land reconciler PR to compute prorated reserved discounts across tag-boundary windows; target ship in next weekly billing patch (related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/reconciler/pull/927). Follow-ups: add a unit test for mid-hour reserve-swap and add a metric (billing.prorate_merged_count) to monitor how often we merge groups. Customer notified and will confirm acceptance of provisional credit before final invoice adjustment.
next_steps: 1) Merge reconciler PR with guard conditions and run staging billing run against synthetic swap data (owner: Arjun Patel, ETA 2026-03-18).
2) Run full reconciliation for March period and compute final credit amount; if different from provisional, issue balancing credit or invoice correction (owner: billing team, ETA 2026-03-20).
3) Add alert for unusual postback tag churn during hourly windows (owner: Observability team, ETA 2026-03-25).
4) Update runbook Confluence page with explicit guidance on reserved swaps and expected billing artifacts (owner: Billing PM, ETA 2026-03-22).
